reply.rationale: No defensible multi-entry compositional paradigm survives the evidence requirements. Recurrent letters/digraphs (e.g. D in D/DC/DS/DT, H in H/HC/HI, P in PI/PS, T in T1–T5) do not show stable, frame-preserving substitution with predictable whole meanings. The T1–T5 family especially fails the opaque-index test: the numerals select different stored procedures rather than contributing literal count meaning compositionally. Standalone symbols such as bot/op/top are meaningful lexical items, but there is no supported multi-morpheme construction in which they alternate in the same slot. Because any proposed segmentation would rely on shared characters or numbering rather than a meaning-consistent substitution paradigm, the safest analysis is a flat lexicon.
